items.title: Why AMI Labs’ Alexandre LeBrun won’t call his AI ‘AGI’ or ‘superintelligence’
items.summary: AMI Labs founder Alexandre LeBrun avoids labeling his artificial intelligence systems as "AGI" (Artificial General Intelligence) or "superintelligence," preferring more cautious terminology around AI capabilities. The distinction reflects a broader debate in the AI industry about how to responsibly describe and discuss advanced machine intelligence development.

items.title: Why AMI Labs’ Alexandre LeBrun won't call his AI 'AGI' or 'superintelligence' | TechCrunch
items.summary: AMI Labs founder Alexandre LeBrun avoids using terms like "AGI" (Artificial General Intelligence) or "superintelligence" to describe his company's AI systems. The article explores LeBrun's reasoning for rejecting these commonly used labels in the AI industry, suggesting a more cautious or precise approach to characterizing the capabilities of his technology.

headline: AMI Labs raises €890M and joins Next40 as LeBrun publicly rejects 'AGI' framing
stateOfPlay: AMI Labs' most consequential week on record: a €890 million fundraise and entry into France's Next40 programme cement it as a flagship of the French AI sector. Simultaneously, co-founder Alexandre LeBrun used the media attention to stake out a deliberate terminological position, refusing to describe the company's systems as AGI or superintelligence. No new hires, publications, or corporate filings were recorded this week, keeping the spotlight squarely on the funding milestone and its narrative framing.

threads.title: €890M raise and Next40 entry mark AMI Labs' arrival as a national AI champion
threads.narrative: AMI Labs has raised 890 million euros and been admitted to France's Next40 programme, according to reporting published on 22 July 2026. The combination of a major capital injection and a place on the government-backed growth index positions AMI Labs alongside the most closely watched French tech companies. The scale of the round makes it one of the largest in French AI history and is expected to substantially expand the company's operational runway.

threads.title: LeBrun's rejection of 'AGI' and 'superintelligence' labels signals a deliberate public positioning
threads.narrative: In a TechCrunch feature published on 16 July, Alexandre LeBrun explained why he avoids the terms 'AGI' and 'superintelligence' when describing AMI Labs' systems, opting for more cautious language about AI capabilities. The stance, articulated at the moment of the company's largest fundraise, appears designed to differentiate AMI Labs from competitors who deploy maximalist framing and to ground public expectations in more precise terms.

evidence.label: TechCrunch: Why LeBrun won't call his AI 'AGI' or 'superintelligence'

signals.text: No new job postings were added this week despite the €890M raise; total open roles remain at 5, with 4 in Technical Staff.
No new research publications or GitHub activity of note were recorded, suggesting the team's public energy this week was directed at the funding announcement.

AMI Labs team member Pascale Fung posted on X defending the value of large industry-funded research, citing Bell Labs, IBM, Xerox PARC, Microsoft, and Google as precedents — a signal consistent with the company's own positioning as a well-capitalised research-driven lab.

Alexandre LeBrun's leadership transition at Nabla — he stepped down, with Brian Manning taking over — was reported on 22 July, separating his personal profile from that company as AMI Labs takes centre stage.
Corporate filings show no change in capital (€12,449.43), no new dirigeants, and no IP filings this week, meaning the fundraise has not yet registered at the Infogreffe level.

whatToWatch: Look for a Kbis or capital update at the corporate registry reflecting the €890M round, and watch whether the Next40 admission accelerates new senior hires or triggers a wave of research publications as the company scales up.
